newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Taiwan cancels, Petron emerges.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Taiwan cancels, Petron emerges.

text.p: Gasoline prices on Wednesday were steady despite Taiwan's decision to cancel its purchase tender as fresh demand emerged from Philippines, traders said.
Both August 92-octane and 95-octane were offered on the Singapore fob market at $22.80 and $23.80 per barrel -- the same levels last talked or traded on Monday.
"The impact (of Taiwan) is marginal because if they buy, it would only be one cargo," said a trader. "And they can't go without buying, and are likely to make up for it in the second-half tender."

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) cancelled its tender to buy 250,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate for delivery between September 1-15 due to high offers, a company official told Reuters.
"We have cancelled because the offers were above $25 (per barrel on a cost-and-freight basis) and we cannot accept it," the official said.
He said the lowest offer, around $25.30 was too high as on Monday, a 95-octane unleaded cargo was traded at $23.80 per barrel free-on-board Singapore.
He said adding $1.00 per barrel for freight to Taiwan, "we can accept below $25".
The latest offers were also much higher than the last CPC award at $23.30 c-and-f Taiwan for delivery August 11-20 from a Dutch trader, traders said.
The offical said there were fewer offers into the tender.
"Usually we receive around 10 offers, this time there were only eight," he said.
"Maybe next week we may issue a new tender," the official said. "We will have to reconsider our position, we may push our refinery througput or we may purchase."
The high offers were also attributed to the 2.0-percent MTBE content in the reformate required.
Asian MTBE prices have hit a year high with September lots traded at $280 per tonne, fob.
Supplies of MTBE in August have already run out while demand was healthy from blenders, endusers and traders interested in taking arbitrage cargoes to the firmer U.S. market.
CPC awarded its tender to buy two 3,500 tonne cargoes of MTBE for September 6-20 delivery from two companies at around $290 per tonne, c-and-f, a company official said.
The award is $20 higher than CPC's last tender award of two cargoes of 3,500 tonnes of MTBE for August 6-20 at $270 per tonne c+f, taking one cargo each from a Mideast and a European producer.
Meanwhile, Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp re-emerged for its gasoline requirements but in a closed tender to selected sellers.
Petron is seeking 100,000 barrels of 95 or 97-octane unleaded reformate for delivery August 10-20 on a cost-and-freight basis to Bataan.
The tender closed on July 28 but results have yet to be announced, a trader said.
Early last week, Petron cancelled its first gasoline import tender in about two years, because of "operational considerations", a company official said.
The cancelled tender which sought 70,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline for August 11-15 delivery, closed on July 18 and was vaild for the day.

Since the cancellation, European major British Petroleum has sold around 100,000 barrels of August delivery 97-octane unleaded gasoline to Petron, through negotiations, at around 60-80 cents per barrel over Singapore 97-octane quotes.
Naphtha firmed with August swaps traded at $22.20 and $22.10 per barrel before prices settled down at $21.95/$22.05, marginally firmer from Tuesday's levels on crude gains.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
